dimensions.note: The television portrait gives a located account of a detective who reaches past his assignment and keeps his discretion. He brings Chisato and Takina a stalking complaint the police are slow on, because Saori may speak more easily to girls (E01). He fends Mitani off with an unspecific answer, then on his own initiative shows him the bullet, explains that incidents have been turned into accidents, judges the chief to be under orders and calls it dangerous to challenge whoever hides so much (E04-E05). He defends silence by asking what it matters who covered up what if a girl like that can live in safety (E05). With an identified suspect he does ordinary police work and presses an uncomfortable question (E12-E13). It predicts his costs and overreach: the referral moves a first interview onto two young people who meet a danger he never named; he decides for himself where Mitani's education stops; and he invokes the safety of a girl whose actual work he cannot see. Not B: the portrait says self-preservation and concern for familiar people can both be genuine reasons, and its closing question is whether he would keep that answer if the person he meant to protect disputed it. Those motives would diverge in exactly the case the portrait leaves open, so this is insufficiency, not productive uncertainty. Each mechanism also rests on a single located instance. Not D: the account is a dedicated, located interpretation with narrow conditional expectations, each tied to a television act and its cost.

Located states: the referral (E01); deflection, then disclosure to Mitani (E04-E05); ordinary police work (E12-E13); a repeated look at the phone image and Mitani turning his いろいろ back on him (E13). The portrait says the lasting change it can see is between the two men, and that Abe gets a second look, not a confession of changed allegiance. Not C: no change in Abe himself is located. Not E: each state is placed by episode and cue.

The only television Japanese form quoted for him is いろいろ あんだよ きっとな, a deliberately unspecific answer to Mitani (E04), which he later repeats when Mitani returns it (E13). Other television speech is rendered in English: asking whether the girls are going to a festival and praising them (E05), wondering aloud whether there are too many middle-aged men (E03), urging Chisato to hurry because his lunch break will end (E07), asking Mitani whether he is already satisfied (E13), urging flight and admitting the trouble with trespassing (E05). The print forms the portrait analyzes are outside scope. Not C: one quoted television form, and the row does not claim speech. Not E: register differences between teaching a colleague and café banter are located.

Located in the television evidence: a café regular the others notice when work keeps him away (E04); joining games on duty and in his lunch break (E03, E07); asking about a daytime drink, which Mitani corrects, without being shown drinking (E08). Not C: no routine or life beyond the café games is located on television. Not E: several distinct habits are located.

Directed differences: Mitani (a junior colleague he first deflects, then teaches and dissuades, and who later turns his own word on him, E04-E05, E08, E13); Chisato and Takina (hired help he pays and later greets and praises; he beckons Takina and does not press her when she declines, E01, E03, E05); Saori, reached only through the referral (E01); Robota (a suspect in custody he presses, E13); the chief (believed to be under orders, E05). Not B: the portrait does not say how his answer would change if a person he means to protect disputed it, and his television relationship with Mika and the staff is barely located. Not D: each relationship has located acts and a stated difference.

Located only as stated reasons: the police are slow and Saori may talk more easily to girls (E01); he cannot tell whether someone is solving the incidents or covering them up, and challenging whoever hides them is dangerous (E05); a girl like that living in safety (E05). The portrait doubts how content either man is at E13 and says the phone image establishes no knowledge or decision. Not C: there is no access to his inner states beyond those reasons. Not E: the reasons are his own and located.

Located modes: deflecting Mitani with an unspecific answer (E04); arguing him out of telling the chief by citing danger and ordinary safety (E05); urging flight when a workman finds them (E05); pressing a suspect who resists exposure (E13); conceding Mitani's ironic point (E13). Not C: each mode occurs once and Mitani's dissatisfaction is never resolved on screen. Not E: the modes are distinct and located with their outcomes.

The row claims ethics. The located position is E05: real danger to anyone who inquires, against the safety of ordinary people he knows, while Mitani finds a different responsibility in the same evidence. The E01 referral is a practical act whose cost the portrait names. Not C: this is one stated position whose deciding motive the portrait leaves open, not a pattern of weighing. Not E: the position and its stated reasons are located.

Located only as brief café banter: too many middle-aged men (E03), the lunch break (E07) and the daytime drink (E08). Not D: the portrait uses these to measure what 'ordinary' means to him and analyzes no pattern of play.

One short dedicated portrait locates every television appearance it relies on by cue and timecode, with four directly inspected E13 stills, and keeps its print comparisons attributed. Not B: about half the portrait is print outside this subject's continuity, his screen time is small, and the row curates only this derived item. Not D: the television appearances relied on are located.

Located bounds against overreading: Saori's danger is discovered by Chisato and Takina, and he neither presents the discovery nor claims credit (E01); he has no demonstrated access to the rest of Chisato's day (E05); E08 does not show him drinking; pressing Robota shows suspicion, not proof that Robota caused the blackout (E13); the E13 phone image does not establish that he can identify the figure, has penetrated DA, or has decided to disclose anything; the prose never supplies his private belief about the girls on television; and the Recovery days rider is an unnamed Kanagawa detective, distinct from television Abe. Not A: no forecast about him is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.
States are placed by episode, cue and timecode. Not B: there is no story calendar for his appearances. Not D: the episode states are precisely located.

scenario_readiness.note: The row does not claim speech. One television Japanese form is quoted for him; the other located speech is rendered in English, and the print forms are outside scope. Located lines may be reported as canon; generated lines are not supported.

conditions: Someone outside his assignment needs a hearing the police are slow to give, and he knows capable regulars: predict a referral with an offer to pay, without naming a danger he has not established (E01). Include the cost: the first contact with danger falls on the people he referred.

A junior colleague questions an official account: predict an unspecific deflection first, then, on his own initiative, showing evidence while arguing against open pursuit, citing danger from whoever hides it and the safety of ordinary people he knows (E04-E05).
An identified suspect or actionable report: predict ordinary police work and a pressing question, without treating suspicion as proof (E12-E13).
Include his mistakes: passing risk to others without naming it, deciding for himself where a colleague's education stops, and invoking the safety of someone whose real situation he cannot see.

Exclude a demand to betray Mika, an objection from the person he means to protect, a verified revelation about Chisato's work, a personally known victim who makes silence untenable, and his private life.

known_limits.statement: The portrait says self-preservation and concern for familiar people can both be genuine reasons for his silence, and leaves open whether he would keep his answer about ordinary safety if the person he meant to protect disputed it (E05; closing paragraph).

About half the portrait draws on separately attributed Asaura prose. Those scenes, his prose age and the print forms are outside the television continuity; the prose never supplies his private belief about the girls on television, and the Recovery days rider is a distinct Kanagawa detective.
The E13 phone image establishes repeated attention, not that he can identify the figure, has penetrated DA, or has decided to disclose anything.
The E01 referral moved a first interview onto two young people who then met a danger he never named; he neither presents their discovery nor claims credit.
Pressing Robota about the blackout shows suspicion, not proof that Robota caused it (E13).
His upbringing, family, intimate life, precise rank and the origin of his friendship with the café staff are undisclosed.
Untested: a demand to betray Mika, a direct objection from Saori to the referral, a verified revelation about Chisato's work, and a personally known victim who makes continued silence untenable.
